name: useHiLight
summary: The eight-LED ring around the rear camera flash. Real LEDs or nothing.
plain: Controls the coloured lights around the rear camera. Useful as a glanceable signal when the phone is face down: a colour for an incoming call, a pulse while an assistant is thinking. Either it drives the physical LEDs or it reports that it cannot; there is no on-screen substitute.
description: Android 17 exposes the array as eight lights of type Light.LIGHT_TYPE_APPLICATION, but every lights session needs CONTROL_DEVICE_LIGHTS, which is signature|privileged and cannot be held by a normal app. PixelKit therefore ships a small Java daemon that runs as the adb shell user and listens on 127.0.0.1:11080; start it with npm run hilight:daemon. With the daemon up, availability is hardware and the calls drive real LEDs. Without it, availability is simulated: the colour and pattern state is still tracked and mirrored on screen with haptics, and nothing pretends the lights are on.

returns.name: availability
returns.desc: Whether calls reach the LEDs ('hardware'), the daemon is not running ('unavailable'), or this device has no array.

returns.name: isHardwareSupported
returns.desc: Whether this device physically has the LED array.

returns.name: isDaemonConnected
returns.desc: Whether the local daemon answered its last status check, polled every five seconds.

returns.name: isActive
returns.desc: Whether the ring is currently lit.

returns.name: currentColor
returns.desc: Active colour as a hex string.

returns.name: mode
returns.desc: Pattern label: off, glow, breathing, pulse, gemini_thinking, incoming_call or notification.

returns.name: brightness
returns.desc: 0 to 1. The hardware has no brightness channel, so this scales the RGB values.

returns.name: isFaceDownMode
returns.desc: Whether glanceable face-down behaviour is engaged.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Where the numbers came from. There is no 'simulated' value: a reading is real, derived from real readings, or unavailable.

actions.name: refreshDaemonStatus()
actions.desc: Re-checks the daemon immediately instead of waiting for the next five-second poll.
actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon answered, false otherwise. The same value lands in isDaemonConnected.

actions.name: setColor(hex)
actions.desc: Sets a solid colour and turns the ring on, switching the mode from off to glow when needed.

inputs.name: hexColor
inputs.desc: RGB hex string such as "#81C995". Sent to the daemon as-is, scaled by brightness.

actions.output: Returns nothing. Nothing lights unless availability is hardware.

actions.name: setMode(mode)

inputs.name: mode
inputs.desc: One of off, glow, breathing, pulse, gemini_thinking, incoming_call, notification. Passing 'off' extinguishes the ring.

actions.output: Returns nothing; mode and isActive update immediately.

actions.name: setBrightness(level)
actions.desc: Scales the RGB values sent to the LEDs. The hardware has no separate brightness channel.
actions.output: Returns nothing. Applied immediately when the ring is lit, stored otherwise.

actions.name: triggerGeminiPulse(ms?)
actions.desc: Cyan gemini_thinking hold that clears itself. Pair it with a model call.

inputs.name: durationMs
inputs.desc: How long to hold before clearing, in milliseconds. Defaults to 4000.

actions.output: Returns nothing. A pending timer from an earlier call is cancelled first.

actions.name: triggerContactAlert(hex, ms?)
actions.desc: Coloured incoming_call hold for a caller or event, then clears itself.

inputs.name: hexColor
inputs.desc: RGB hex for the alert colour.

inputs.name: durationMs
inputs.desc: Hold time in milliseconds. Defaults to 5000.

actions.output: Returns nothing. Replaces any hold already running.

actions.name: turnOff()
actions.desc: Clears the ring and cancels any pending auto-off timer.
actions.output: Returns nothing; mode becomes off and isActive false.

actions.name: toggle()
actions.desc: Switches between off and a default blue glow.

agentNote: Read availability before promising light. Only 'hardware' drives the LEDs; 'unavailable' means the daemon is not running and the control functions refuse rather than pretending.
